prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1013; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection and stated they were stopped at the light when their vehicle was struck from behind. They are not represented by counsel and have asked for the claim to be handled directly.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver reporting the loss is named on it and the coverage was active at the time of the incident. Police report and both drivers' statements have been requested.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who described the collision the same way the claimant did. Two witnesses at the scene have been contacted, and photos taken on the day show rear-end damage consistent with the reported impact. Police confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle when officers arrived.

Entry 4: Claimant reports neck and back pain beginning the day of the accident and has provided medical records showing a back strain diagnosis. The injury fits the force and direction of the collision, and no prior treatment to the same area is known from the records or the claimant's history.

Entry 5: A neighbor mentioned seeing the vehicle with body damage several weeks before the claimed loss date. This has been noted for follow-up, and the claimant has been asked to clarify any earlier damage to the vehicle. No prior damage has been recorded on file so far.

Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far. Medical treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as recovery progressed, and the vehicle damage estimate is largely in line with the described impact. Claim is progressing with the neighbor comment still open for review.
